target.title: fix(agents): cancel pending bundle LSP requests when the agent stops
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who stopped an agent while a bundle-provided LSP hover, definition, or references tool was pending could still leave the language server working for up to the request timeout and receive a late tool result after the run had been cancelled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bundle LSP tools now pass their per-call abort signal into the JSON-RPC request owner. Aborting removes that request from the pending map, clears its timer and listener, rejects the tool promise, and sends the LSP-standard `$/cancelRequest` notification for the same request id. The shared language-server process is intentionally kept alive for other calls.

## User Impact

Stopping an agent now stops its pending bundle LSP tool calls promptly. The language server can cancel the corresponding work, late responses no longer resolve the cancelled tool call, and other tools can continue using the same server session.

## Evidence

Reporter-provided pre-fix live proof used Claude bundle discovery, `.lsp.json`, a real stdio child process, and Content-Length JSON-RPC framing. The aborted hover call did not send cancellation and resolved 602 ms after abort:

```json
{
  "lspCancelRequestReceived": false,
  "settledWithin100msAfterAbort": false,
  "toolResolved": true,
  "settledAfterAbortMs": 602,
  "serverRespondedAfterAbort": true
}
```

Post-fix local E2E live proof drives the same production surfaces and also verifies the shared server handles another request after cancellation:

```json
{
  "realClaudeBundleLoaded": true,
  "materializedTool": "lsp_hover_prooflive",
  "runSignalAborted": true,
  "lspRequestReceivedBeforeAbort": true,
  "lspCancelRequestReceived": true,
  "settledWithin100msAfterAbort": true,
  "toolResolved": false,
  "settledAfterAbortMs": 1,
  "serverRespondedAfterAbort": true,
  "sharedSessionSurvived": true
}
```

Focused regression suite:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  11 passed (11)
```

Additional checks:

- `oxfmt --check` passed for both touched files.
- Repository `run-oxlint.mjs` passed for both touched files.

  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format.   • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

4.35.3 - 01 May 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.19.3 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 9 April 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.15, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3837
  • Configurations for private registries that use Cloudsmith or GCP OIDC are now accepted. #3850
  • Best-effort connection tests for private registries now use GET requests instead of HEAD for better compatibility with various registry implementations. For NuGet feeds, the test is now always performed against the service index. #3853
  • Fixed a bug where two diagnostics produced within the same millisecond could overwrite each other on disk, causing one of them to be lost. #3852

target.title: fix(tools): reject malformed availability expressions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`ToolDescriptor` availability is typed in TypeScript, but external JavaScript can still provide malformed runtime values. The existing shallow key check can throw on nested primitives, overflow on cycles, or let sparse groups evaluate as available.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Validate availability expressions recursively before evaluation, including required signal fields and group arrays.
- Treat the `WeakSet` as the active recursion stack so true cycles are rejected while shared sibling expressions remain valid.
- Materialize array indices during validation so sparse groups and config paths cannot skip checks.
- Preserve existing behavior for absent availability and the precise empty-`allOf` / empty-`anyOf` diagnostics.

The submitted ten-file callback/cache/plugin design was replaced with this evaluator-owned path. Current plugin availability is manifest-first; adding a second runtime-tool availability contract and repeated hot-path logging would recreate an ownership model removed from `main`.

## User Impact

Malformed or cyclic descriptors now fail closed with the existing `unsupported-signal` diagnostic instead of throwing, overflowing, or exposing a tool. Valid descriptors and public types are unchanged; there is no new config, callback, cache, or plugin API.

## Evidence

- Regression coverage for explicit `null`, malformed signals/groups, ambiguous shapes, sparse groups/paths, true cycles, shared children, and precise empty-group diagnostics.
- `oxfmt` on both changed files; `git diff --check` clean.
- Three autoreview passes; the first two found and drove fixes for explicit-null and sparse-array fail-open paths. Final pass: clean, 0.94 confidence.
- Exact-head sanitized AWS tests, changed gate, package build, and packed public-SDK consumer proof are running against `53ceb54b6a712bb1e3fffe818ef4c24ca7f5f3ab`.

No changelog entry: `CHANGELOG.md` is release-owned in this repository.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve UTF-16 boundaries in block chunks
target.body:
## Summary

- preserve UTF-16 boundaries when `EmbeddedBlockChunker` must split at `maxChars`
- keep fence close/reopen handling aligned with the adjusted split index
- add production-class regressions for plain, fenced, and one-code-unit budgets

## What Problem This Solves

When no natural Markdown break existed, the chunker returned the raw UTF-16 code-unit `maxChars` index. If that index fell between an astral character's high and low surrogates, the emitted chunk ended with an isolated high surrogate and the buffered remainder began with an isolated low surrogate.

## User Impact

Streamed block chunks no longer contain malformed UTF-16 when a forced size boundary lands inside emoji or another astral character.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows:** #104030, which preserved UTF-16 pairs in Twitch outbound chunks.
- **Gap this fills:** the shared embedded-agent block chunker independently used forced code-unit indices before its local emit boundary.
- **Consistency:** forced chunk boundaries now reuse the repository's shared `sliceUtf16Safe` utility.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

A fresh exact-class search found #94216 and #94247 touching the same chunker files, but both address paragraph-separator preservation. Their diffs append or coordinate `\n\n` around paragraph breaks and do not align forced `maxChars` indices to UTF-16 boundaries. #68986 does not change the chunker source or target test.

No open PR covers the surrogate-boundary root cause, and the author's open PR scan found no overlap.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** malformed chunk strings can render as replacement characters or fail later text handling.
- **Risk labels considered:** session-state and streamed-text.
- **Risk explanation:** a split can move one code unit earlier when `maxChars` bisects a surrogate pair. For the otherwise impossible `maxChars=1` case with an astral first character, the complete two-unit code point is emitted so the chunker retains forward progress.
- **Why acceptable:** normal budgets remain hard upper bounds; only a one-unit budget can be exceeded by one code unit because no valid non-empty UTF-16 chunk can contain half of a surrogate pair.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High; the production class is directly reproducible and all forced branches share one adjusted index.

target.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a restricted agent could create a recurring cron job with a trigger script and a `systemEvent` payload, then have that script receive the full coding tool surface. Main-session cron jobs require `systemEvent`, so the common path bypassed the creator's tool policy whenever cron triggers were enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The creator tool cap now applies whenever a cron job has a trigger script, in addition to isolated `agentTurn` jobs. The cap is retained on every cron payload shape, survives updates, is persisted through the cron SQLite store so it survives a gateway restart, and is passed to the headless trigger evaluator. This keeps the existing agent-turn behavior while covering main-session system events and command payloads.

Distinct from #12736, which concerns global cron deny policy; #97317 and #101349, which concern isolated agent-turn defaults; and #41484, which concerns elevated execution scope.

## User Impact

Agents restricted to a small tool set can use cron triggers without acquiring shell, exec, or patch capabilities beyond that set. Existing unrestricted operator-created cron jobs continue to work with their configured policy.

## Evidence

- `node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed: 144 checks.
- `node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.cron.config.ts src/cron/normalize.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed: 59 checks.

## Real behavior proof

```
{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"changed"}
# AFTER (this patch, head 711292119844c93e432a3b39b8897f31dbf92750, identical input)

```

target.title: fix(agents): preserve UTF-16 boundaries in bootstrap context
target.body:
## Summary

- preserve UTF-16 boundaries in generic and `AGENTS.md` bootstrap head/tail retention
- add a production-entry regression covering both surrogate split directions in both trimming paths
- reuse the shared `sliceUtf16Safe` helper without changing bootstrap budgets or markers

## What Problem This Solves

Bootstrap context trimming preserved the beginning and end of oversized workspace files with raw UTF-16 code-unit slices. When either boundary landed inside an emoji or another astral character, `EmbeddedContextFile.content` could contain an isolated high or low surrogate.

## User Impact

Oversized bootstrap files containing astral characters at retention boundaries no longer inject malformed text into locally built embedded-agent context.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows:** #104047, which preserved UTF-16 boundaries in workshop previews.
- **Gap this fills:** bootstrap context independently retained generic and `AGENTS.md` heads/tails with raw `String.prototype.slice` calls.
- **Consistency:** all four retention slices now use the repository's shared UTF-16-safe slicing utility.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

A fresh competition scan found no open PR changing `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/bootstrap.ts`, the target regression test, or the exact `buildBootstrapContextFiles` entrypoint behavior.

#89894 only reorders the documented `AGENTS.md` template and explicitly does not change truncation logic, `bootstrapMaxChars`, or content-aware trimming. The author's open PR scan found no overlapping implementation.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** malformed UTF-16 in bootstrap context can render as replacement characters or fail later text handling.
- **Risk labels considered:** session-state and prompt-context.
- **Risk explanation:** when a configured retention boundary splits a surrogate pair, that side can now contain one fewer UTF-16 code unit than its numeric budget.
- **Why acceptable:** dropping an incomplete surrogate half preserves valid text while retaining the existing head/tail allocation, policy digest, marker, and total-budget behavior.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High; the production entry is directly reproducible and the patch reuses the existing shared helper.
- **Patch quality notes:** focused two-file patch with no type escape, fallback, public contract change, dependency change, or unrelated refactor.
- **Target test file:** `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts`
- **Root cause:** both generic and `AGENTS.md` trimming paths formed internal retained substrings with raw UTF-16 code-unit slices before the final safe overall clamp.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** all four source boundaries are corrected before malformed substrings can enter marker rendering or `EmbeddedContextFile.content`.
- **What did NOT change:** per-file and total limits, allocation ratios, compact/full marker selection, policy digest selection, warning behavior, missing-file handling, schemas, and public APIs remain unchanged.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `trimBootstrapContent` and `trimAgentsBootstrapContent` are the source of truth for retained bootstrap substrings; no downstream consumer or model adapter was changed.
- **Scenario locked in:** a generic 300-code-unit file whose `74+24` retention splits two emoji, plus a 1,000-code-unit `AGENTS.md` file whose `270+90` retention splits two emoji.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** one production-entry table test exercises head and tail boundaries in both canonical trimming branches and inspects the returned context object.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** truncated generic and `AGENTS.md` bootstrap content no longer contains isolated surrogate halves at retained head or tail boundaries.
- **Canonical reachability path:** input → schema/type `WorkspaceBootstrapFile` → ingestion `buildBootstrapContextFiles` → normalization `normalizeOptionalString` and bootstrap trimming → runtime object `EmbeddedContextFile` → returned `content` effect. Concretely, workspace file content enters `WorkspaceBootstrapFile.content`, receives a per-file budget, passes through generic or `AGENTS.md` head/tail rendering and the total-budget clamp, then returns as `EmbeddedContextFile.content`.
- **Boundary crossed:** the production entry ingests canonical workspace bootstrap file objects and returns the local runtime `EmbeddedContextFile[]`; the proof terminates at that returned production object.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** reused `sliceUtf16Safe` through the existing shared utility export; provider-specific constraints are not applicable.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix
- **Real environment tested:** Linux worktree on Node 22 with the repository pnpm toolchain.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** direct `buildBootstrapContextFiles` execution for generic, `AGENTS.md`, and ASCII-control fixtures, plus `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts`.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
BEFORE generic: lone high surrogate U+D83D at output index 73; lone low surrogate U+DE00 at index 175
BEFORE AGENTS:  lone high surrogate U+D83D at output index 269; lone low surrogate U+DE00 at index 382
AFTER generic:  complete head=73, complete tail=23, output length=197, marker preserved
AFTER AGENTS:   complete head=269, complete tail=89, output length=470, marker preserved
CONTROL:        short ASCII bootstrap remained unchanged
TESTS:          1 file passed, 25 tests passed
```

- **Observed result after fix:** both returned truncated contexts contain only complete UTF-16 pairs, preserve their branch-specific read-full-content markers, remain under configured limits, and retain the expected complete ASCII head/tail controls.
- **What was not tested:** downstream model consumption was not exercised; this defect and proof terminate at the locally returned bootstrap context object.

## Regression Test Plan

- run `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts`
- verify both trimming branches remove isolated high and low surrogate halves
- verify existing policy-digest, tiny-budget, total-cap, missing-file, and ASCII paths remain green

## Risk / Compatibility

No API, schema, configuration, or dependency changes. A retained side can be one code unit shorter only when the previous boundary split a surrogate pair.

## Out of scope

No changes to workspace file discovery, configuration parsing, policy-digest prioritization, prompt assembly after bootstrap construction, model adapters, or downstream consumption. The task commit changes only the production trim source and its focused regression test; unrelated paths shown by a two-dot comparison are newer `origin/main` drift, not part of this PR.

## Root Cause

The final `truncateUtf16Safe` clamp protected only the end of the fully rendered string. It could not repair isolated surrogate halves already created by internal raw head/tail slices, so each source slice must preserve UTF-16 boundaries before rendering.

target.title: fix(duckduckgo): forward the execution abort signal to web search HTTP requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling an agent run while a DuckDuckGo `web_search` request is pending leaves that HTTP request running, and the shared provider loop can start another provider after cancellation. The parent execution signal reaches the generic web-search runtime, but the shared fallback loop treats parent abort like an ordinary provider error and continues to the next candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a two-layer root-cause fix:

1. **Provider layer (DuckDuckGo):** Forward the `AbortSignal` from the tool execution context through the provider to the guarded endpoint helper (`withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint`), which already accepts a signal parameter.

2. **Shared runtime layer** (`src/web-search/runtime.ts`): Add `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` before each candidate provider attempt and treat `params.signal?.aborted` as terminal in the catch path (`params.signal?.aborted || !allowFallback`). This prevents the shared fallback loop from starting another provider after the user cancels the run — the same canonical fix from SearXNG PR #104216 (zhangguiiping-xydt, 🦞 diamond lobster).

The change does not alter DuckDuckGo configuration, schemas, caching, timeouts, SSRF policy, provider ordering, ordinary-error fallback, or response formatting. Regression coverage locks both the signal handoff and the no-fallback-after-abort behavior.

## User Impact

Cancelling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight DuckDuckGo search without starting another provider. Normal completed searches, cached results, and ordinary provider-error fallback are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Focused test suite (44 tests across 3 files)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    src/web-search/runtime.test.ts \
    extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-search-provider.test.ts \
    extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-abort-proof.test.ts \
    --reporter=verbose

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  44 passed (44)
```

### Key regression coverage

- **"does not fall back to another provider after parent cancellation"** (`runtime.test.ts`): firstExecute called once, fallbackExecute never called, rejects with `AbortError`. Canonical no-fallback-after-abort test from #104216.
- **"forwards the execution abort signal through guarded fetch to the HTTP request"** (`ddg-abort-proof.test.ts`): Exercises the FULL production chain — `runDuckDuckGoSearch` → `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `globalThis.fetch`. Only `fetch` is mocked; the real SSRF guard, DNS policy, redirect loop, and timeout-abort wrapper all run. Signal captured from `RequestInit.signal` at the fetch layer, abort listener registered, `controller.abort()` triggers `DOMException("The operation was aborted")`, test verifies rejection. Matches Brave (#104269) and SearXNG (#104216) proof pattern.
- **"forwards the execution abort signal to the DuckDuckGo client"** (`ddg-search-provider.test.ts`): Verifies `controller.signal` reaches `runDuckDuckGoSearch` via `context.signal` from the provider.
- **Ordinary-error fallback preserved:** "falls back when auto-selected provider returns structured error" and "does not fall back when provider came from explicit config selection" still pass.

### Shared runtime fix (2 lines, same pattern as #104216)

```diff
 for (const candidate of candidates) {
+  params.signal?.throwIfAborted();
   try {
     ...
   } catch (error) {
     lastError = error;
-    if (!allowFallback) {
+    if (params.signal?.aborted || !allowFallback) {
       throw error;
     }
   }
```

### Non-goals (unchanged)
- No changes to DuckDuckGo configuration, schemas, caching, timeouts, SSRF policy, response formatting
- No changes to explicit provider selection behavior
- No changes to ordinary-error fallback (preserved)
- No dependency, lockfile, config, protocol, or changelog changes

### Patch quality
- 5 files: 3 source + 3 test (1 new proof file)
- Source +7, Tests +118. Total +125. 7 deletions.
- No new API surface, no config surface, no dependency changes.
- oxlint: clean on changed files.

target.title: fix(gateway): cap history when numeric limit is huge
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway HTTP session history treated an all-digit `limit` above JavaScript's safe integer range as invalid and returned the minimum one-message page instead of the endpoint's bounded maximum history window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The parser now distinguishes malformed or zero values from numeric overflow, then relies on the existing `MAX_SESSION_HISTORY_LIMIT` clamp. Because the endpoint cap is 1,000, precision above that cap is immaterial: finite unsafe numbers and `Infinity` have the same bounded result. This removes the submitted extra branch while preserving one canonical limit path.

## User Impact

## Summary

- preserve UTF-16 boundaries in context-pruning head and tail retention
- add a production-path regression test covering both surrogate split directions
- reuse the shared `sliceUtf16Safe` helper without changing pruning budgets

## What Problem This Solves

Soft context pruning preserves the beginning and end of long tool results. The previous joined-text helpers used raw UTF-16 code-unit slices, so a head boundary could retain only an emoji's high surrogate while a tail boundary could begin with only its low surrogate.

## User Impact

Long tool results containing emoji or other astral characters at pruning boundaries can no longer produce malformed text in the rewritten agent context.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows:** #103789, which made saved-view text truncation UTF-16 safe.
- **Gap this fills:** context pruning independently retained tool-result heads and tails with raw `String.prototype.slice` calls.
- **Consistency:** both pruning directions now use the repository's shared UTF-16-safe slicing utility.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

A fresh competition scan found two open PRs touching only the adjacent test file:

- #99532 tests that text-only tool results remain text during pruning, but it does not exercise surrogate boundaries or modify `pruner.ts`.
- #98441 adds a thinking-settings fixture field, but it does not modify text truncation behavior.

Neither PR changes the unsafe head/tail helpers or covers this UTF-16 root cause. Exact `pruneContextMessages` search and the author's open PR scan found no competing implementation.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** malformed UTF-16 in rewritten context can render as replacement characters or fail later serialization.
- **Risk labels considered:** session-state.
- **Risk explanation:** when a pruning boundary splits a surrogate pair, that retained side can contain one fewer UTF-16 code unit than before.
- **Why acceptable:** dropping an incomplete surrogate half preserves valid text while retaining the existing head/tail policy and configured budgets.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High; the production entry is directly reproducible and the patch reuses an existing shared helper.
- **Patch quality notes:** focused two-file patch with no type escape, fallback, public contract change, or unrelated refactor.
- **Target test file:** `src/agents/agent-hooks/context-pruning/pruner.test.ts`
- **Root cause:** the text-normalization invariant was violated because both joined-text helpers used raw UTF-16 code-unit slices that could split surrogate pairs.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the source boundary is corrected inside the canonical head and tail retention helpers, before malformed substrings can enter the rewritten runtime message.
- **What did NOT change:** only surrogate-boundary handling changed; pruning thresholds, character budgets, image markers, trim notes, hard-clear behavior, schemas, and public APIs remain unchanged.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `takeHeadFromJoinedText` and `takeTailFromJoinedText` are the source of truth for soft-pruning retention; no downstream serializer or model adapter was changed.

- **Canonical reachability path:** input source `toolResult.content[].text` from an existing agent message → ingestion/type handling in `pruneContextMessages` and `collectTextSegments` → joined-text normalization and soft-trim budget calculation → runtime head/tail strings → rewritten `AgentMessage` effect returned by the production entry.


- **What was not tested:** later model-consumption stages were not exercised; this defect and proof terminate at the returned production message object.

N/A — new focused follow-up with no existing review findings.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes web-search credential presence detection so the audit only reports usable web-search credentials after applying plugin policy, selected provider scoping, and provider-specific env/auth contracts.

target.title: fix(agents): lease session worktrees during runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A resumed session's managed git worktree could be deleted out from under an active agent run. Idle GC, a separate remover, or a manual `worktrees.gc` would remove the session's isolated checkout while the run was still using it, destroying in-flight workspace files. The silent counterpart also existed: a session whose managed worktree had already been removed was admitted anyway and ran as if its cwd were an ordinary directory, with no checkout.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a rewrite of the earlier approach after maintainer review. The earlier head used a process-local FIFO lease, which was an exclusive full-run mutex (a parent and a child run sharing one worktree could deadlock), leased only `cwd` (a workspace-only child was unprotected), and leaned on `git worktree lock` as the admission/removal mutex even though that lock is not an atomic cross-process check-and-act.

Runs now take a shared run-lease and removal takes an exclusive claim, both stored as rows in the existing shared-state `state_leases` table. Admission and removal each run inside one `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction`, which uses `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (`src/infra/sqlite-transaction.ts`), so the read-check-write is serialized across processes by SQLite itself. That single transaction is the atomic admission/removal gate, replacing the git-lock TOCTOU. The git worktree lock is kept only as a secondary raw-Git guard, refcounted per process so a parent and a same-process child do not unlock each other.

Each lease row carries an opaque token plus `pid` and process start time. Run leases and the removal claim are both token-owned: a run releases only its own token, and the removal claim rejects a competing live remover and clears or finalizes only under its own token, so two removers can never enter destructive work on the same worktree at once. Dead or reused-pid owners, including a removal claim whose remover process died before finalizing, are pruned inside the same transaction via `isLockOwnerDefinitelyStale`, so a killed holder never strands the worktree. The worktree id is resolved from the session's stored `worktree.id` binding, or by containment over both the run cwd and workspace dir, so a workspace-only child still leases. Removal claims before any cleanliness or snapshot work and rejects while a live run lease exists.

Choosing the shared state DB over sidecar claim files follows the repository storage policy (SQLite only for runtime registries), and reuses the same cross-process lease table and transaction primitive already used by startup-migration checkpoints.

## User Impact

Users resuming sessions with isolated worktrees can no longer have their live checkout deleted underneath an active run by idle GC, a manual gc, or session cleanup, including when the session works in a subdirectory of the worktree and including when a second process races the removal. A session whose checkout was removed while it was away now fails fast with a clear error instead of silently continuing without its files. Concurrent parent and child runs can share one worktree without deadlocking, and two removers cannot corrupt a worktree by deleting it concurrently.

## Evidence

- Branched off `origin/main` `cba9ffb1`; head `07a34750`. Mergeable, behind current main.
- Focused suites pass (39 in the worktree group): `src/agents/worktrees/run-lease.test.ts` and `src/agents/worktrees/service.remove-lease.test.ts` cover parent/child shared readers with git-lock refcounting, the workspace-only child id resolution, dead-owner (SIGKILL) pruning, reused-pid (ABA) pruning, force parity, admission-fails-once-removing, dead-remover recovery, exclusive rejection of a second live remover (with and without force), owner-scoped abort that cannot clear a newer claim, a concurrent second remover rejected at the service level, and gc skipping a busy worktree; existing `service.test.ts` still passes. `agent.test.ts`, `agent.session.test.ts`, and the gateway worktrees/session-create/session-delete-lifecycle/server-maintenance suites pass unchanged.
- `oxlint --type-aware` and `oxfmt --check` clean on all changed files; `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` clean.
- Two pre-ship Codex reviews were addressed: the first flagged a stranded removal marker after a mid-removal crash (fixed by the self-healing pid/start-time owner); the second flagged that the removal claim was overwritable and its cleanup was not owner-scoped (fixed by the opaque token, exclusive rejection, and owner-scoped abort, with regressions).

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a resumed session's managed worktree must survive a concurrent separate-process non-force removal while its run is active; a session whose managed worktree was already removed must fail admission instead of running without its checkout; and two removers must not enter destructive removal of the same worktree at once.
Real environment tested: two real OS processes sharing one on-disk git worktree, the real `ManagedWorktreeService` removal path, and the real shared-state SQLite lease store, driven on pristine `origin/main` `d5fe0c5e73` versus this patch `07a34750` with identical inputs; a genuine second node process holds the run lease while the parent issues the removal, and a second overlapping removal is issued against the real service.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node --import tsx proof-lease.mts`, which creates a real session-owned git worktree with a nested workspace file, spawns a separate node process that acquires the run lease, issues a non-force `ManagedWorktreeService` removal from the parent while that process holds the lease, releases and re-removes, removes a second worktree and attempts admission for its path, then starts one removal of a third worktree and issues a second overlapping removal against the same service.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine origin/main d5fe0c5e73)
separate-process run holder: run holds no lease
separate non-force removal during the live run: removed=true
nested session workspace file survived the removal attempt: false
removal after the run ends: rejected: unknown active worktree: 49d88e6b-9b04-4c47-a9e3-c442cdbaa77d
admission for an already-removed managed worktree: no admission guard exists on this tree
second remover racing the first: rejected: git worktree remove failed: fatal: '.../proof-concurrent' is not a working tree
# AFTER (this patch 07a34750, identical inputs)
separate-process run holder: run holds a lease
separate non-force removal during the live run: rejected: worktree is busy: locked by live pid 3058766
nested session workspace file survived the removal attempt: true
removal after the run ends: removed=true
admission for an already-removed managed worktree: admission fails with: managed worktree was removed: /tmp/openclaw-proof-0mB5iH/state/worktrees/f506dd45dc6f28d7/proof-removed
second remover racing the first: rejected: worktree removal is already in progress
```
Observed result after fix: while a separate process holds the run lease, a non-force removal is rejected as busy and the run's uncommitted workspace file survives, then succeeds only after the run ends; a second remover racing the first is rejected as already in progress; on the base the same first removal deletes the live checkout and its in-flight file, the second remover instead collides with the first into a corrupt half-removed worktree, and admission for an already-removed worktree proceeds with no guard.
What was not tested: no live provider request, gateway deployment, or multi-host run was exercised; the processes ran on the development Linux host sharing one state directory and git worktree, so cross-process protection rests on the directly exercised SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE serialization plus the on-disk git worktree lock; the parent/child shared-reader, dead-owner recovery, reused-pid, force-parity, workspace-only, and owner-scoped-abort cases are covered by the regression suite rather than this harness.

target.title: fix(duckduckgo): forward the execution abort signal to web search HTTP requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling an agent run while a DuckDuckGo `web_search` request is pending leaves that HTTP request running, and the shared provider loop can start another provider after cancellation. The parent execution signal reaches the generic web-search runtime, but the shared fallback loop treats parent abort like an ordinary provider error and continues to the next candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a two-layer root-cause fix:

1. **Provider layer (DuckDuckGo):** Forward the `AbortSignal` from the tool execution context through the provider to the guarded endpoint helper (`withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint`), which already accepts a signal parameter.

2. **Shared runtime layer** (`src/web-search/runtime.ts`): Add `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` before each candidate provider attempt and treat `params.signal?.aborted` as terminal in the catch path (`params.signal?.aborted || !allowFallback`). This prevents the shared fallback loop from starting another provider after the user cancels the run — the same canonical fix from SearXNG PR #104216 (zhangguiiping-xydt, 🦞 diamond lobster).

The change does not alter DuckDuckGo configuration, schemas, caching, timeouts, SSRF policy, provider ordering, ordinary-error fallback, or response formatting. Regression coverage locks both the signal handoff and the no-fallback-after-abort behavior.

## User Impact

Cancelling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight DuckDuckGo search without starting another provider. Normal completed searches, cached results, and ordinary provider-error fallback are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Focused test suite (44 tests across 3 files)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    src/web-search/runtime.test.ts \
    extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-search-provider.test.ts \
    extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-abort-proof.test.ts \
    --reporter=verbose

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  44 passed (44)
```

### Key regression coverage

- **"does not fall back to another provider after parent cancellation"** (`runtime.test.ts`): firstExecute called once, fallbackExecute never called, rejects with `AbortError`. Canonical no-fallback-after-abort test from #104216.
- **"forwards the execution abort signal through guarded fetch to the HTTP request"** (`ddg-abort-proof.test.ts`): Exercises the FULL production chain — `runDuckDuckGoSearch` → `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `globalThis.fetch`. Only `fetch` is mocked; the real SSRF guard, DNS policy, redirect loop, and timeout-abort wrapper all run. Signal captured from `RequestInit.signal` at the fetch layer, abort listener registered, `controller.abort()` triggers `DOMException("The operation was aborted")`, test verifies rejection. Matches Brave (#104269) and SearXNG (#104216) proof pattern.
- **"forwards the execution abort signal to the DuckDuckGo client"** (`ddg-search-provider.test.ts`): Verifies `controller.signal` reaches `runDuckDuckGoSearch` via `context.signal` from the provider.
- **Ordinary-error fallback preserved:** "falls back when auto-selected provider returns structured error" and "does not fall back when provider came from explicit config selection" still pass.

### Shared runtime fix (2 lines, same pattern as #104216)

```diff
 for (const candidate of candidates) {
+  params.signal?.throwIfAborted();
   try {
     ...
   } catch (error) {
     lastError = error;
-    if (!allowFallback) {
+    if (params.signal?.aborted || !allowFallback) {
       throw error;
     }
   }
```

### Non-goals (unchanged)
- No changes to DuckDuckGo configuration, schemas, caching, timeouts, SSRF policy, response formatting
- No changes to explicit provider selection behavior
- No changes to ordinary-error fallback (preserved)
- No dependency, lockfile, config, protocol, or changelog changes

### Patch quality
- 5 files: 3 source + 3 test (1 new proof file)
- Source +7, Tests +118. Total +125. 7 deletions.
- No new API surface, no config surface, no dependency changes.
- oxlint: clean on changed files.

target.title: fix(browser): reject hex click coordinates in act route
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where direct Browser `/act` callers sending `clickCoords` could pass hexadecimal coordinate strings such as `"0x10"`, and the route would coerce them into unintended numeric positions instead of rejecting the invalid input.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Browser action route now uses the existing strict route finite-number parser for both `clickCoords.x` and `clickCoords.y`, matching the Browser CLI coordinate contract while preserving decimal coordinate strings such as `"42.5"`. The old permissive route-only numeric helper was removed so this boundary has one canonical parser.

## User Impact

Browser agents and direct Browser control callers get a clear invalid-request response for hex coordinate strings, instead of silently clicking a coerced coordinate.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Browser `/act` rejects hex string coordinate values for both `clickCoords.x` and `clickCoords.y`, while decimal-string coordinates still perform a real coordinate click through the Browser control server.
- Current head: `acbb44838ae95a9d8fac96f99d5ecfd99c9d83a4`.
- Real Browser behavior proof: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` started the branch's authenticated loopback Browser bridge with a temporary managed Chromium profile, then drove real HTTP `/start` and `/act` requests. The bearer token and ephemeral ports were redacted from the public transcript.

```json
{
  "head": "acbb44838ae95a9d8fac96f99d5ecfd99c9d83a4",
  "start": { "status": 200, "ok": true },
  "setup": {
    "status": 200,
    "ok": true,
    "result": { "left": 30, "top": 30, "width": 120, "height": 80 }
  },
  "decimalClick": { "status": 200, "ok": true, "url": "about:blank" },
  "clickedReadback": { "status": 200, "ok": true, "result": "1" },
  "hexX": {
    "status": 400,
    "code": "ACT_INVALID_REQUEST",
    "error": "x must be a finite number."
  },
  "hexY": {
    "status": 400,
    "code": "ACT_INVALID_REQUEST",
    "error": "y must be a finite number."
  }
}
```

- Focused regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/server.agent-contract-core.test.ts -- --testNamePattern "coordinate|navigation \\+ common act"` passed with 1 file, 4 tests passed, and 21 skipped.
- Formatting: `node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.CMD --check --threads=1 extensions\browser\src\browser\routes\agent.act.normalize.ts extensions\browser\src\browser\routes\utils.ts extensions\browser\src\browser\server.agent-contract-core.test.ts` passed.
- Branch diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: the real Browser control server accepted `x: "42.5", y: "64"`, clicked a live button inside the managed Chromium page, and read back click count `"1"`; the same real `/act` route rejected `x: "0x10"` and `y: "0x10"` with `ACT_INVALID_REQUEST` before dispatch.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the Browser `/act` normalization path, the existing strict numeric route helper, the Browser CLI coordinate contract, open self PR occupancy, and the adjacent open Browser PR #104094, which covers a different existing-session target-refresh invariant.

target.title: fix(workboard): scope default positions by board
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users creating Workboard cards on separate boards could see the default card order on one board offset by cards that only exist on another board.

## Why This Change Was Made

Workboard create now allocates implicit card positions inside the final normalized board scope and status, including board ids supplied through either top-level create fields or metadata automation. Explicit positions, status ordering, idempotent create behavior, and board stats remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Workboard boards keep independent default card ordering, so the first todo card on each board starts at the expected position and later cards advance within that board only.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: default Workboard create positions are scoped by board for both top-level `boardId` and `metadata.automation.boardId` inputs.
- Current head: `6e7feec9444ed0deace2f508dbf2aa1dc1df1c57`.
- Real Workboard runtime proof: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` with a repo-local transcript importing `createWorkboardTools`, `workboard_create`, `WorkboardStore.create`, and `createWorkboardSqliteStores`, then closing/reopening SQLite and reading back through `WorkboardStore.list`.

```json
{
  "head": "6e7feec9444ed0deace2f508dbf2aa1dc1df1c57",
  "proofPath": [
    "createWorkboardTools",
    "workboard_create",
    "WorkboardStore.create",
    "createWorkboardSqliteStores",
    "close/reopen SQLite",
    "WorkboardStore.list"
  ],
  "observed": {
    "toolCreates": [
      { "boardId": "ops", "title": "ops first", "status": "todo", "position": 1000 },
      { "boardId": "product", "title": "product first", "status": "todo", "position": 1000 },
      { "boardId": "product", "title": "product second", "status": "todo", "position": 2000 }
    ],
    "storeMetadataCreates": [
      { "boardId": "metadata-board", "title": "metadata first", "status": "todo", "position": 1000 },
      { "boardId": "metadata-board", "title": "metadata second", "status": "todo", "position": 2000 }
    ],
    "persistedAfterReopen": [
      { "boardId": "metadata-board", "title": "metadata first", "status": "todo", "position": 1000 },
      { "boardId": "metadata-board", "title": "metadata second", "status": "todo", "position": 2000 },
      { "boardId": "ops", "title": "ops first", "status": "todo", "position": 1000 },
      { "boardId": "product", "title": "product first", "status": "todo", "position": 1000 },
      { "boardId": "product", "title": "product second", "status": "todo", "position": 2000 }
    ]
  },
  "assertions": {
    "opsFirstStartsAt1000": true,
    "productFirstStartsAt1000": true,
    "productSecondAdvancesTo2000": true,
    "metadataFirstStartsAt1000": true,
    "metadataSecondAdvancesTo2000": true,
    "persistedAfterReopen": true
  },
  "ok": true
}
```

- Focused regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts -- --testNamePattern "scopes idempotent creates and stats by board"` passed with 1 test and 78 skipped on this head.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: refactor(agents): converge CLI tool terminal reason onto run-termination
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The one-shot and live CLI runners each derived the same terminal decision — `timed_out` / `cancelled` / `failed` for tools when a run ends — with different logic:

- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.ts` (one-shot) read the abort signal's lifecycle fields, then only recognized `FailoverError` timeouts; a `TimeoutError`-shaped or `AbortError`-shaped run error without an aborted signal classified as `failed`.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.ts` (live) only sniffed error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) and never consulted the abort signal.

Because the live path trusted the delivered error's name alone, a run timeout whose abort reason reached the turn as a generic `AbortError` (or a non-`Error` timeout reason, which `createAbortError` cannot preserve) was reported as `cancelled` instead of `timed_out`; conversely a user cancel racing a timeout-shaped provider error reported `timed_out` where the one-shot path reports `cancelled`. Same decision, two encodings, observable drift — seam 3 of #104219.

## Why This Change Was Made

Converge the derivation onto one owner, per the #104219 change shape. `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` lives in `src/agents/run-termination.ts` — the module that already owns abort→stop-reason semantics (`resolveAgentRunAbortLifecycleFields`) — and encodes one rule: abort-signal lifecycle fields are authoritative when the signal has aborted; error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) classifies otherwise. Both call-site derivations are deleted in the same change; the live turn now carries the run's real abort signal (`ClaudeLiveTurn.abortSignal`, threaded in `createTurn`).

`terminalReason` feeds diagnostic events only (`tool.execution.error` category/reason fields), so behavior changes are contained to diagnostics classification. The per-site `errorCategory` vocabularies (`timeout/aborted/error` vs `aborted/cli_tool_incomplete/cli_tool`) intentionally differ per event source and stay site-local.

## User Impact

Tool-failure diagnostics now classify consistently across CLI runner modes:

- Live runs that hit the run timeout report `timed_out` (previously `cancelled` when the abort reason arrived as a generic `AbortError` or a non-`Error` reason).
- A user cancel racing a timeout-shaped error consistently reports `cancelled` on both paths (signal wins).
- One-shot runs with a `TimeoutError`/`AbortError`-shaped run error and no aborted signal now report `timed_out`/`cancelled` instead of `failed`.

No control-flow, retry, or delivery behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Drift sites and trace: old derivations at `execute.ts` (`resolveToolTerminalReason`) and `claude-live-session.ts` (`failActiveClaudeLiveTools`); live abort delivery via `createAbortError(signal.reason)` loses timeout identity for generic/non-`Error` reasons.
- Tests: table-driven matrix for `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` in `src/agents/run-termination.test.ts` (11 cases), including both drift regressions: "timeout abort wins over generic AbortError" and "cancel abort wins over timeout-shaped error".
- Local: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:import-cycles` all exit 0; focused vitest green (`run-termination`, cli-runner suites — 270+ tests).
- Remote (Blacksmith Testbox, leases `tbx_01kx80mneqrn7dyntk6cjptc4t`, `tbx_01kx837g6z39m9kjrfkr8mvsm8`), branch rebased on latest `main`: `pnpm check:changed` exit 0. `pnpm test:changed` hit two known-flaky failures under full parallel shard load (`model-fallback.probe.test.ts` async log-capture assertion; `Worker exited unexpectedly` on the gateway shard); both pass in isolation on the same lease and diff — probe test 20/20 twice, full gateway shard 402 files / 6454 tests green. Neither touches this diff's surface.
- `git diff --numstat`: +43/−17 prod, +96 tests. Net prod +26 buys the single owner: both call-site derivations deleted, one closed union exported.

### Real behavior proof (ephemeral runtime)

Real `executePreparedCliRun` flow — production executor, real process supervisor spawning a real child process, real `claude-stream-json` parser — with a stub CLI backend (one JSONL `mcp_tool_use` line, then silence; no network, no API keys, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`). Events observed on the trusted tool-execution bus (`onTrustedToolExecutionEvent`; the public `onDiagnosticEvent` filters trusted events). One-shot path exercised; the live session consumes the same shared helper.

Timeout run (no-output watchdog → `FailoverError reason:"timeout"`), redacted:

```json
{
  "type": "tool.execution.error",
  "runId": "run-proof-timeout",
  "toolName": "mcp__openclaw__cron",
  "toolOwner": "cli-runner",
  "toolCallId": "call-proof-timeout",
  "durationMs": 1509,
  "errorCategory": "cli_tool_incomplete",
  "terminalReason": "timed_out"
}
```

User-cancel run (`abortController.abort()` after `tool.execution.started` → `AbortError` with aborted signal), redacted:

```json
{
  "type": "tool.execution.error",
  "runId": "run-proof-cancel",
  "toolName": "mcp__openclaw__cron",
  "toolOwner": "cli-runner",
  "toolCallId": "call-proof-cancel",
  "durationMs": 137,
  "errorCategory": "aborted",
  "terminalReason": "cancelled"
}
```

**Claude-live path** (same harness family, routed through `shouldUseClaudeLiveSession`: backend id `claude-cli`, `liveSession: "claude-stdio"`; stub waits for the live turn's stdin input, emits a tool use, holds the session; log lines confirm `claude live session start/close reason=abort`). Both events emitted by `failActiveClaudeLiveTools` and carry `toolOwner: "claude-cli"`, exercising the newly threaded `ClaudeLiveTurn.abortSignal`:

Timeout abort — the exact drift case this PR fixes: signal aborted with a non-`Error` timeout reason (`{ name: "TimeoutError" }` → lifecycle `stopReason: "timeout"`), while `createAbortError` delivers a generic `AbortError("CLI run aborted")`. Pre-fix live classification (error shape only) would say `cancelled`; captured after-fix event:

```json
{
  "type": "tool.execution.error",
  "runId": "run-live-proof-timeout",
  "toolName": "mcp__openclaw__cron",
  "toolOwner": "claude-cli",
  "toolCallId": "call-live-timeout",
  "durationMs": 116,
  "errorCategory": "timeout",
  "terminalReason": "timed_out"
}
```

User cancel (plain `abort()` while the live tool is active):

```json
{
  "type": "tool.execution.error",
  "runId": "run-live-proof-cancel",
  "toolName": "mcp__openclaw__cron",
  "toolOwner": "claude-cli",
  "toolCallId": "call-live-cancel",
  "durationMs": 123,
  "errorCategory": "aborted",
  "terminalReason": "cancelled"
}
```

Branch rebased on current `main`; focused tests + `tsgo:core` green post-rebase.

Part of #104219 (seam 3: CLI-runner terminal reason derivation).

target.title: feat(xai): add native streaming TTS
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Add native xAI WebSocket streaming TTS through the existing `streamSynthesize` speech-provider contract.

This is separate from xAI realtime voice. It preserves the provider's existing buffered TTS, voice discovery, authentication, and telephony behavior.

## Behavior

- Streams from the canonical `wss://api.x.ai/v1/tts` endpoint.
- Rejects non-canonical streaming bases before bearer-authenticated WebSocket setup, including altered ports, credentials, paths, queries, and fragments.
- Sends ordered `text.delta` frames within xAI's 15,000-character limit, without splitting Unicode surrogate pairs, followed by `text.done`.
- Decodes `audio.delta`, completes on `audio.done`, and propagates server errors.
- Bounds encoded WebSocket frames and cumulative decoded audio.
- Refreshes the idle timeout for every audio chunk.
- Handles close-before-open, cancellation, completion, and repeated `release()` safely.
- Uses existing language, voice, codec, and speed controls; xAI defaults apply to sample rate and bit rate.

The existing Discord caller may deliberately fall back to buffered synthesis when a stream fails. Discord voice requests MP3 through a stream-only xAI provider override, including when a persona is active, while preserving the configured codec for buffered fallback. Other streaming callers retain all five xAI codecs.

## Evidence

Exact head: `f08d1fd20df3002d515869adf952529cce6986fd`

```text
Focused provider tests
  extensions/xai/tts.test.ts
  extensions/xai/speech-provider.test.ts
  extensions/discord/src/voice/manager.e2e.test.ts
Result: 3 files, 179 tests passed

Test typecheck
  pnpm check:test-types
Result: passed

Full repository check in Crabbox
  pnpm check
Result: passed
  preflight/package/security guards: passed
  core + extensions typecheck: passed
  core + extensions + scripts lint: 0 warnings, 0 errors
  policy/import-cycle guards: passed

Official live provider test with a real XAI_API_KEY
  node scripts/test-live.mjs -- extensions/xai/xai.live.test.ts \
    -t "synthesizes TTS through the registered speech provider"
Result: 1 passed, 8 unrelated live cases skipped
The test drained a real stream, asserted output metadata and byte count,
and released the provider stream.

git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
Result: passed

Codex autoreview, gpt-5.5 high
Result: 0 actionable findings; patch is correct (confidence 0.82)
```

An independent current-head review found and eliminated two codec-boundary regressions before publication: restricting valid xAI codecs at the provider boundary, and allowing persona config to override Discord's stream-only MP3 selection. No actionable provider implementation, endpoint, lifecycle, dependency, or lockfile finding remains.

## Dependency

`ws@8.21.0` already existed as an xAI plugin development dependency. This change moves it to runtime dependencies because the production streaming implementation imports it. The dependency guard may therefore require maintainer approval.

## Scope

This PR does not add realtime voice, change buffered TTS behavior, alter Discord's existing fallback decision, expose sample-rate/bit-rate controls, or add a custom xAI proxy. It only makes Discord's streaming request use MP3 while leaving buffered fallback configuration untouched.

No API keys, tokens, credentials, private paths, raw prompts, or raw agent logs are included.

## Agent Transcript

<details>
<summary>Sanitized multi-day engineering worklog</summary>

This lane has been active since at least July 3, 2026. It was not produced in a single short pass.

### Iteration history

- Started from the native xAI `/v1/tts` WebSocket contract and the existing OpenClaw speech-provider boundary.
- Added ordered text framing, Unicode boundary handling, bounded payloads, cumulative audio limits, timeout refresh, and lifecycle cleanup.
- Corrected invalid `RawData` test fixtures found by the full test typecheck.
- Tightened endpoint validation after independent security review showed that host-only validation accepted altered URL shapes.
- Rebased and reconstructed the lane in clean worktrees while preserving commits after Windows junction issues affected disposable checkouts.
- Ran focused tests, test typecheck, full repository checks in Crabbox, independent review, Codex autoreview, and finally the official live provider test with a real credential.

### Strongest safe truth

The exact head is test-proven across focused and full repository checks and runtime-proven for registered-provider native xAI streaming TTS. It is not claimed as a live Discord end-to-end proof, and it does not change Discord's pre-existing buffered fallback policy.

</details>

target.title: fix(line): AI-assisted - requireMention can now optionally gate non-text messages with bounded pending-media retention
target.body:
Closes #103758

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where LINE groups configured with `requireMention: true` could not require a mention before non-text messages (image/video/audio/file) reached the agent. Any photo, video, voice clip, or file posted in such a group was always processed, regardless of whether the bot was actually mentioned, because LINE's Messaging API never attaches mention metadata to non-text messages and the mention-gate logic could not account for that.

Fixes an issue where operators of mention-gated LINE groups would see the bot react to every image/video/audio/file dropped in the chat, even when nobody addressed the bot, when they expected the same "must be mentioned" behavior that already applies to text messages (per #34438 / #35847).

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds two new **opt-in** LINE group config fields — `requireMentionForNonText` and `pendingMediaLimit` — so operators can explicitly turn on mention gating for non-text messages without changing default behavior for anyone else. Because LINE never reports a mention on the non-text message itself, a bounded per-group pending-media queue (default limit 3) retains the most recent skipped media until a later message in the same group is mentioned and fully processed, at which point the queued media is attached to that turn and the queue is cleared. This lets a user post a photo, then follow up with `@bot look at this`, and have the photo still reach the agent.

A prior attempt at the opt-in flag alone (#68197) went stale without merging and did not include the retention queue, which meant skipped media was simply dropped forever once a group opted in — this PR keeps the same opt-in, default-false posture that maintainers asked for on #68197, and adds the missing retention piece on top.

## User Impact

LINE operators can now set `channels.line.accounts.<id>.groups.<groupId>.requireMentionForNonText: true` (alongside `requireMention: true`) to require an `@mention` before non-text messages reach the agent, matching the existing text-message behavior. Skipped media isn't lost — up to `pendingMediaLimit` (default 3) recent items are retained per group and delivered alongside the next mentioned message. Existing configs are unaffected since both fields default to off/unset.

## Evidence

`pnpm test:extension line` — 26 test files, **313 tests passing** (up from 307 on `main`; +6 in `bot-handlers.test.ts`, +2 in `config-schema.test.ts`):

```
 Test Files  26 passed (26)
      Tests  313 passed (313)
```

New tests cover:

- unmentioned non-text message is skipped when `requireMentionForNonText` is set (and the pre-existing "allows non-text through by default" test is preserved unchanged, proving no default-behavior change);
- pending-queue eviction bounded by `pendingMediaLimit` (oldest dropped first);
- queued media flushed into `allMedia`/`processMessage` context on a later mentioned message, then the queue is cleared;
- default `pendingMediaLimit` of 3 when unset;
- schema acceptance of both new fields and rejection of non-positive `pendingMediaLimit`.

Additional local validation:

- `npx tsc -p extensions/line/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean, exit 0
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/line` — 0 warnings/errors

- `node scripts/format-docs.mjs --check` / `markdownlint-cli2` / `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs` — all clean on `docs/channels/line.md`
- `codex` CLI was not available in this environment, so `codex review --base origin/main` could not be run locally; noting this per CONTRIBUTING.md instead of skipping silently.

target.title: fix(perplexity): forward the execution abort signal to web search HTTP requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling an agent run while a Perplexity `web_search` request is pending leaves that HTTP request running. The parent execution signal reaches the generic web-search runtime, but the Perplexity provider discards the execution context, so the request can remain open and eventually resolve after cancellation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the `AbortSignal` from the tool execution context through the provider to the guarded endpoint helper (`withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` / `withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint`), which already accepts a signal parameter.

The change does not alter Perplexity configuration, schemas, caching, timeouts, SSRF policy, provider ordering, or response formatting. A focused test verifies the signal handoff.

Sibling PRs applying the same pattern: SearXNG (#104216 by zhangguiiping-xydt, 🐚 platinum hermit), Brave (#104269), plus the companion PRs filed alongside this one. The Google/Gemini provider already forwards the signal and serves as the reference.

## User Impact

Cancelling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight Perplexity search instead of consuming network and server resources until the configured timeout or response. Normal completed searches and cached results are unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused suite passes on the rebased head, including the signal-forwarding test.

target.title: feat(write): add append mode to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The write tool always overwrites files. An `append: true` parameter lets the agent add content to the end of an existing file instead of replacing it. The agent requested this capability repeatedly in real sessions — it wants to write logs, build up checklists incrementally, and extend existing scripts without re-reading them first.

## Why This Change Was Made

Write-tool silent data loss (#40001) can happen when an agent writes to a file it has already edited without re-reading the current content. An append mode gives the agent a safer option: it can add new content without risking the loss of previous edits.

## What Changed

- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.ts` — add `append?: boolean` to the schema, `WriteOperations.appendFile` method, append branch in `execute`, append-aware recovery (`isRecoveredAppendContent`), and post-mutation abort check matching `edit.ts:460-463`.
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-contracts.ts` — add `append?: boolean` to `WriteToolInput`.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts` — wire `appendFile` for host (`fs.appendFile`), workspace (`root.append()`), and sandbox (read-modify-write, since the sandbox bridge has no native append).
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts` — 7 new tests covering: basic append, append-to-new-file, no-op short-circuit for overwrite, malformed append param rejection, append-identical-content preserving duplicates, append-after-abort recovery via readback, and abort-surfaced-when-append-did-not-persist.

## User Impact

- `append: true` is opt-in. The default write behavior is unchanged.
- Append to a non-existent file creates it (matching `>>` shell semantics).
- The write tool description and prompt snippet advertise the new parameter.

## Evidence

Focused suite (local fallback — Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

Tests cover: basic append, append-to-new, no-op detection for identical overwrite, malformed `append` param rejection, append identical content (duplicate tail preserved), reject append when the custom backend omits `appendFile`, post-mutation abort recovery for append (readback confirms content landed), and abort surfaced when appendFile returned without persisting.

target.title: feat(anthropic): add claude-haiku-4-5 to claude-cli catalog
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Claude CLI catalog and setup allowlist do not include `claude-haiku-4-5`, so OpenClaw users running the local Claude CLI backend cannot select the full Haiku 4.5 model ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR adds Haiku 4.5 to:

- the Claude CLI default allowlist and aliases
- the Claude CLI catalog label, using the existing 200K default context
- the static plugin manifest with a 200K context window, 64K max output, and 1568px image input
- the Claude CLI setup/migration expectations so existing configuration flows seed the model

Fable is intentionally left to #101453. Mythos is intentionally excluded because current `main` exposes it through the direct Anthropic provider rather than the Claude CLI backend.

## User Impact

`openclaw models list --all --provider claude-cli` can expose `claude-cli/claude-haiku-4-5`. Setup/config migration seeds the ref, and both `haiku-4.5` and `claude-haiku-4-5` normalize to the full model id.

## Evidence

### Authenticated OpenClaw-to-Claude-CLI turn

Verified on Windows with Claude Code 2.1.206, using the exact PR head `61dd215e53d50dcefe78b99075ef9764e241b6cf` (`OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (61dd215)`). The OpenClaw state/config was isolated for the proof; the existing Claude Code subscription login was reused. No credentials, session ids, local paths, or hashes are included below.

Catalog probe:

```console
$ pnpm openclaw models list --all --provider claude-cli --json
{
  "key": "claude-cli/claude-haiku-4-5",
  "name": "Claude Haiku 4.5 (Claude CLI)",
  "input": "text+image",
  "contextWindow": 200000,
  "available": true,
  "missing": false
}
```

Agent probe used the current canonical configuration shape: model `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` with model-scoped `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`.

```console
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main \
    --model anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 \
    --thinking off \
    --message "Return exactly OPENCLAW_HAIKU_AGENT_PROOF_OK and nothing else." \
    --json
```

Redacted result:

```json
{
  "payload": "OPENCLAW_HAIKU_AGENT_PROOF_OK",
  "executionTrace": {
    "winnerProvider": "claude-cli",
    "winnerModel": "claude-haiku-4-5",
    "attempts": [
      {
        "provider": "claude-cli",
        "model": "claude-haiku-4-5",
        "result": "success"
      }
    ],
    "fallbackUsed": false,
    "runner": "cli"
  },
  "completion": {
    "finishReason": "stop",
    "stopReason": "completed",
    "refusal": false
  }
}
```

The live backend log independently recorded `provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-4-5` for the successful turn.

### Static and CI proof

- Plugin manifest parses successfully and contains exactly one new Fable/Haiku/Mythos-family Claude CLI row: `claude-haiku-4-5`
- Verified manifest metadata: 200K context, 64K max output, 1568px image input
- Node 24 syntax checks passed for the changed TypeScript files
- Scoped `git diff --check` passed
- [GitHub CI run 286641](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29104973348) passed on the exact head; CodeQL, OpenGrep, Workflow Sanity, and iOS Periphery also passed

target.title: fix(feishu): retry transient message send failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu text, card, image, or file messages could be dropped when `im.message.create` or `im.message.reply` encountered a transient network or server failure. Retrying these ambiguous failures without an idempotency key could also create duplicate messages when Feishu accepted the first request but its response was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu message create/reply calls now opt into two retries for transient transport errors, HTTP 408/425/5xx responses, and the existing rate-limit cases. Each logical send generates one Feishu `uuid` outside the retry closure and reuses it for every attempt, so recovery remains idempotent. Non-idempotent image/file uploads and Card Kit entity creation remain single-attempt operations.

## User Impact

Feishu users should receive messages reliably through short-lived DNS, connection, timeout, and server failures without duplicate text, cards, or media messages. Permanent API errors still fail immediately, and upload behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- Live Feishu service proof (`2026-07-11T09:43:26Z`): sent a uniquely marked message to a private bot DM through the real Feishu API. After Feishu accepted attempt 1, the proof harness deliberately threw `ECONNRESET` to simulate a lost response. The production retry wrapper made attempt 2 with the same UUID; Feishu returned the same message ID, and a real chat-history query found exactly one matching delivered message.

```json
{
  "environment": "real Feishu API and private bot DM",
  "controlledFailure": "ECONNRESET thrown after Feishu accepted attempt 1",
  "attempts": 2,
  "uuid": "186f...7320",
  "firstAcceptedMessageId": "om_x...e2ab",
  "retryMessageId": "om_x...e2ab",
  "sameMessageId": true,
  "chatId": "oc_0...23ce",
  "historyMatchCount": 1,
  "matchingMessageIds": ["om_x...e2ab"],
  "exactlyOneDelivered": true,
  "result": "PASS"
}
```

- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.reply-fallback.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts`
- Observed after the patch: a transient first `message.create`/`message.reply` attempt rejects, the second succeeds, and both captured SDK calls contain the same UUID. The focused suite passed `5 files / 157 tests`.
- Upload boundary proof: a transient `image.create` failure invokes the upload exactly once and never invokes `message.create`, confirming non-idempotent uploads are not replayed.
- Full Feishu suite after rebasing onto current `upstream/main`: `79 files / 1146 tests` passed.
- Type checks: extension source and extension test tsgo projects passed.
- Static checks: targeted oxfmt, targeted oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- SDK contract: pinned `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.68.0` declares `data.uuid?: string` for both `im.message.create` and `im.message.reply`.
- The proof uses a controlled post-acceptance `ECONNRESET` instead of disrupting the production network. This exercises the ambiguous delivery case directly while keeping the live Feishu service and private DM as the delivery and de-duplication boundary.

AI-assisted: Codex helped implement and review this change; the branch was locally verified as listed above.

Related: #90804

target.title: fix(discord): add timeouts to directory lookup requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord directory, user allowlist, and channel allowlist lookup requests could hang indefinitely when Discord API fetches stalled before headers or during response body reads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Directory lookup callers now pass a focused 10 second timeout into the existing Discord API helper. The helper keeps the timeout alive through both `fetch()` and bounded response body reading, then clears it after the request attempt settles.

## User Impact

Discord configuration and lookup flows fail quickly when Discord API lookup calls stop responding, instead of blocking target resolution and directory browsing.

## Evidence

Exact head after normal merge from `upstream/main`: `c1e37ab5beb0c38a40632c43f4aa72bce32cc6a3`. The merge was a normal merge commit; no rebase or force-push was used.

Validation run:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/api.test.ts extensions/discord/src/directory-live.test.ts
-> 2 files passed, 22 tests passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/resolve-users.test.ts extensions/discord/src/resolve-channels.test.ts
-> 2 files passed, 21 tests passed

git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD -- extensions/discord/src/api.test.ts extensions/discord/src/api.ts extensions/discord/src/directory-live.test.ts extensions/discord/src/directory-live.ts extensions/discord/src/guilds.ts extensions/discord/src/resolve-channels.ts extensions/discord/src/resolve-users.ts
-> clean

node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 extensions/discord/src/api.ts extensions/discord/src/api.test.ts extensions/discord/src/directory-live.ts extensions/discord/src/directory-live.test.ts extensions/discord/src/guilds.ts extensions/discord/src/resolve-channels.ts extensions/discord/src/resolve-users.ts
-> clean
```

Controlled stalled Discord API proof run:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module
```

Harness shape: local HTTP server simulating Discord API responses, production `listDiscordDirectoryGroupsLive()` runtime path, production `fetchDiscord()` / `requestDiscord()` helper, and global fetch routed only from `https://discord.com/api/v10/*` to the local server. The proof uses normal HTTP fetches and a redacted Discord bot token; it does not use mocked response streams.

Observed behavior:

- Normal Discord directory lookup succeeds before and after the stalled cases.
- A channel lookup that stalls before response headers aborts in about 10 seconds and closes the server-side request/response.
- A channel lookup that stalls while reading the JSON response body also aborts in about 10 seconds and closes the server-side request/response.
- This exercises the production Discord directory lookup runtime and the shared Discord API helper rather than a unit-only mocked stream.

Known limits:

- This is controlled-network runtime proof, not a live Discord API outage reproduction.
- Remote Testbox/Crabbox proof was unavailable in this environment because no working `crabbox` binary was present; this used the documented narrow local fallback plus GitHub CI.

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
